answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by making every wallet that submits work lock a stake in a registry, counting weight per locked unit, not per address. A swarm of fake agents must fund each wallet separately, so a thousand identities cost a thousand stakes. Stakes stay exposed to slashing: if the cluster votes alike on disputed work, a challenge tears it apart and burns the collateral. The attacker pays full price per identity plus risk of losing it all, while an honest participant risks one terrace of value. Splits leave a ferrous trace, so graders cut noise as a prism splits light.
